entries.title: Readiness in Motion- how 726 EMSS TMO keeps operations on track (9759459).jpg
entries.description: U.S. Air Force Senior Airman Sepesa Taukete, 726th Expeditionary Mission Support Squadron Traffic Management Office journeyman, transports cargo at Camp Lemonnier, Djibouti, June 16, 2026. TMO personnel use material handling equipment to safely move and stage inbound cargo, ensuring mission-essential assets are rapidly distributed to supported units or processed into supply systems supporting operations throughout the Horn of Africa. (U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Luis Gomez)
entries.creator: U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Luis Gomez

entries.title: Readiness in Motion- how 726 EMSS TMO keeps operations on track (9759472).jpg
entries.description: U.S. Air Force Senior Airman Sepesa Taukete, 726th Expeditionary Mission Support Squadron Traffic Management Office journeyman, verifies inbound materiel against shipping manifests at Camp Lemonnier, Djibouti, June 16, 2026. Before any asset is processed into the Integrated Logistics System-Supply, TMO personnel conduct rigorous visual inspections to ensure 100% accountability and zero receipt discrepancies transforming inbound freight into actionable mission assets. (U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Luis Gomez)

entries.title: NASA Portal Details Land Motion Across North America (PIA26494 figA).jpg
entries.description: NASA, along with the agency's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California, is collaborating with the Alaska Satellite Facility in Fairbanks to create a powerful web-based tool that will show the movement of land across North America down to less than an inch. The online portal and its underlying dataset unlock a trove of satellite radar measurements that can help anyone identify where and by how much the land beneath their feet may be moving – whether from earthquakes, volcanoes, landslides, or the extraction of underground natural resources such as groundwater. Spearheaded by NASA's Observational Products for End-Users from Remote Sensing Analysis, or OPERA, project at JPL, the effort equips users with information that would otherwise take years of training to harness. The project builds on data from spaceborne synthetic aperture radars, or SARs, to generate high-resolution data on how Earth's surface is moving. Formally called the North America Surface Displacement Product Suite, the new dataset dates to 2016. By the end of 2025, the data will cover the entire United States, Central America, and Canada within 120 miles (200 kilometers) of the U.S. border. The image shows how the portal visualizes land sinking over time in Freshkills Park, which is being built on a former landfill on Staten Island, New York. Landfills tend to sink over time as waste decomposes, compacts, and settles under its own weight. The blue dot marks the point on the land where the portal is displaying movement in the accompanying scatterplot. Figure A Click on image for larger version Figure A shows the portal's visualization of uplift, or land rising, at the outlet of the Colorado River to the Gulf of California. As above, the blue dot marks the point for which the portal is displaying movement in the scatterplot. Figure B Click on image for larger version Figure B shows a visualization of land movement near the city of Willcox, Arizona. The region is part of an area in which groundwater use is being managed by the Arizona Department of Water Resources. To access the portal: https://displacement.asf.alaska.edu/ For more about OPERA: https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/go/opera/
entries.creator: Alaska Satellite Facility

entries.title: Old Downtown Post Office, exterior views, 2019 - DPLA - 4304c7cfd2ede8cc17657e999f439754 (page 18).jpg
entries.description: These images are exterior views of a building originally constructed as the downtown branch of the United State Post Office in Toledo. The building has also been owned and used by Toledo Public Schools. The building was designed by J. Knox Taylor, and construction ran from 1909 to 1911. The photographs were taken on April 2, 2019.
entries.creator: Dewees, John Michael
